product_title: Handy Living Wood Slat Bed Frame Extra Long Twin
review_body:
This was easy to put together. We actually bought one for our king and when we got a queen mattress, opted for the queen version of this slat frame because we liked the king one so much.

Pros:
Affordable frame
Easy to put together (we used a rubber mallet, just make sure your aim is true)
No squeaking noises
Feels sturdy.
The vaulted ceiling (from a cat's POV) is awesome. My cats love to lounge under the bed because they can walk without crouching.

Cons
Some slats looked less sturdy (knotty?), but moving them to an area that would receive more stress than another is a work around. So far, none have broken and thus we don't expect. Just as with any bed, jumping up and down like a trampoline is not recommended.

product_title: Zinus SC-SBBK-14NT-FR Smartbase Bed Frame Metal, Narrow Twin
review_headline: Great bed frame for past 2 years!
review_body:
When I first bought this, I was thinking "cheap bed frame for the guest room", but as fate would have it, I ended up using it for myself for the last two years and I've been very happy with it. It has been very comfortable and held up well over that time. I even have a little bit of a tricky back and this has done quite well for that. Along with the mattress I bought it has been very comfortable, not "squeaky", and held up well...including when my kids jump on it. We put our mattresses and frames to the test in my house. :)

In fact, the reason I came back to this page to review is we had to get another bed frame and so I'm buying another one of these.

I also like that it is super easy to assemble. It takes about 10 minutes with no tools other than your hands and yet is still very sturdy after assembled. Equally, it's easy to dissemble and store without taking up a lot of room.

All in all a really great bed frame at a great price.

review_headline: Update: after 7 months this mattress sags. My back and shoulders ache. I feel like I'm sleeping in a hole.Would not recommend.
review_body:
I live on an island so I did as much research as I could to find a suitable mattress. I knew I could not test it so I relied on Consumer Reports and other reviews. I weigh over 250 pounds and needed a firmer mattress. I have had this mattress for 2 weeks now and I keep expecting it will break in. It has not. It is extremely firm to the point that I might as well sleep on the floor. I have ordered a 4" mattress topper to see if that will help. As of now, my arms fall asleep on my side and my back hurts when I lay on my back.
The mattress is well built although the plastic corners are stapled on with small staples and 2 were completely off when the mattress arrived. It is sturdy on the edges. The box spring is very light while the mattress is very heavy. This took almost 6 weeks to arrive. The original order was damaged in shipping and the replacement costs $98.00 more since the original company did not have any more in stock. The original company compensated me. Amazon took no responsibility~sad considering they make a profit.

review_body:
Bought this mattress as something that I could temporarily sleep on while away from home on a 3 month assignment. I figured it was memory foam so it'd be decent and at $179 (at the time of this writing), what could go wrong? Answer: my back. I've had nothing but back problems all summer after sleeping on this mattress. Rather than buy this, sleep on an air mattress or a couch until Woot.com has a memory foam mattress on sale. Alternatively, step up and get one that's at least 10" thick (the one I have at home is 12" and I love it - fixed my back problems in one night).

If you're looking for a "decent" mattress to put in the guest room, this might suffice. But again, I'd suggest you look elsewhere.

product_title: Serta Pearce Pillow Top Mattress
review_headline: Plush Pillow Top That Gives Cloud-Like Sleep
review_body:
Having reviewed many ship-to-home mattresses, this is the first one that is shipped as-is, not rolled up stuffed in a box. This, then, will be similar to a real mattress buying experience like your local mattress shop. The usual mattress-in-a-box on Amazon are, in most cases, significantly lower in price than a typical mattress and, as such, the strong 'need' to test it out before hand is greatly reduced as well. You simply want a mattress, the price is low, therefore you give some of the 'risk' up to get more convenience.

With this Serta Pearce mattress this is not the case. The price is above-average, and it will likely be a 'serious' purchase for you. For this reason, I will concentrate on the sleep of the mattress so that you can make this decision armed with better than average information. I will say that I will, indeed, mention the quality however it will be very light because that is the least worry here--the mattress is made extremely well and it exudes throughout the entirety of the mattress, from the seams at the floor, through the handles on the side, to the pillow-top layer. There is no skimping here.

Firstly, whether or not this is labeled as a firm mattress or not, the sleep quality is plush, period. The pillow-top itself is thick enough to take the bulk of your weight so you really don't ever get to the actual mattress. The pillow-top is squishy. I weigh around 190 lbs and laying on the bed the impression in the pillow-top sank to about 3.5". Yes, again, it's a softy. My preference for a mattress is extremely firm and so this mattress was too soft for me and left my aching after a sleep. However, this is a not a negative as many people like a softer mattress. This being said, the scale of firmness I would rate it 3/10, and categorize the feeling as a Moderate-to-strong plush.

**If you prefer firm mattresses, you will not like the sleep of the Serta Pearce**

The quality of the mattress needs the least said for it as there is nothing to say except that it is very good. Multiple people, upon seeing it for the first time, have all commented without my prompting that it has a uniquely well-made, and attractive mattress. There are two handles on each side of the mattress that is fully canvased and sewed on for easy carry.

For weight, the mattress is fairly heavy and is somewhat hard to maneuver because it folds in on itself fairly easily--very soft throughout, and not stiff. You will need two people if you want to carry it off ground.

You will receive this mattress from a freight company, likely in the back of a semi truck trailer. It is completely wrapped in plastic so that marks from moving will likely not be there. However, check the mattress out before receiving to check for any damage or stains.

---------------------------------------------

The reason for paying the price for this mattress for many of the online 'buy-in-the-box' varieties, is because you want a quality, permanent sleeping solution. product_title: Sleep Innovations Shiloh Memory Foam Mattress
review_body:
How desperately I wanted to like this mattress.

We can talk about firmness and temperature, but what really matters is: how does it affect the quality of my waking life? The answer is: most days, my back is sore when I get up, and I am in general more lethargic which is probably due to poor quality sleep.

If I had to pinpoint a reason, it would be the HEAT. I call this thing the frying pan. I learned on the first night to not use a down comforter (something I used year round with our Beautyrest). I bought a thin cotton blanket, and even that is too warm: many nights I wake up drenched in sweat; other nights I simply find that I have soaked the pillow (sometimes two of them). This can't be good for deep sleep.

Apparently, this is a problem for *some* people with *all* memory foam mattresses, even the expensive ones. (Judging from the reviews here, I'm guessing we are a small minority of the population.) In my hours of online research, I learned that there is no simple fix for dealing with the heat. There are plenty of long forum threads on the topic, with solutions ranging from expensive sleepwear to expensive wool mattress pads to... keeping the windows open or the A/C on all night. I tried the cheapest recommendation, which was to sleep *above* the down comforter so it insulates me from the mattress. That works pretty well at keeping the heat down--though nowhere near as cool as springs were--but is so thick along with the fitted sheet that it defeats the whole memory foam thing. Feels more like a futon pad.

I was hoping that in the ten years since my last mattress purchase, our civilization would have transcended the unpleasant experience of setting foot inside a mattress store (why are they all like visiting a car dealership?), and that may be the case with one of the many mail-order mattress companies out there--but it wasn't with this mattress. I'm not willing to buy another foam mattress sight unseen, so it's back to springs for me.springs for me.

product_title: Marriott Hotel Bed - Foam Mattress & Box Spring - Official Marriott Bed
review_headline: Buying a Marriott (Jamison) Mattress After Dec 2014? DON'T....and here's why!
review_body:
The positive ratings are accurate....but only if you've purchased this bed BEFORE 2014. Now, it's barely worth the money. Here's why.

Prior to 2014, the only hotels that I would stay in were the Marriott brand hotels. When it comes to beds I knew that the Fairfield Inns would occasionally have the comfortable Jamison beds, the Staybridges would frequently have some variation of the Jamison mattresses (always comfortable) and the Marriott and Residence Inns would always have the famous Jamison mattresses! Since my career required that I travel, I pretty much know their mattresses! :)

Well, last year (Dec 2014) I ordered my mattress from the Marriott.com website. I had the model number of the bed that I wanted because I pretty much harassed the managers of housekeeping at 2 nearby Marriott hotels for this information! At first I called Jamison Mattresses and noticed that the greeting no longer said "Jamison Mattresses" like it did the month before when I called. The person who answered told me that Jamison Mattresses was bought out by another company but they were still selling the REMAINDER of the mattresses that they custom made for the Marriott. They told me that they had a specific number that I needed to call in order to buy it. So I called that number and was forwarded to the Marriott.com website. I specifically asked the people at Marriott.com whether or not they were still selling the Jamison mattresses that they've ALWAYS supplied the hotels with. I was told that they did. I placed my order (which was over 2K) along with the mattress padding and was told that I would receive my bed in 2 weeks. My padding came within 3 days and at the end of about 2 weeks I called to find out when my bed was coming so that I could make arrangements to be here. That's when I was told that there was a "holdup" at the factory and that they were still "making" my mattress! 'Wait. What???? Why would they .....?' At this point I asked them why they were "making" my mattress when Jamison said that they were selling the remainder of the mattresses! Why wasn't I getting a mattress that they'd premade in a warehouse because if this was truly a Marriott mattress then that would mean that they were already made and waiting for an order from one of the Marriott hotels, right? Afterall, I highly doubted that they would wait for a order from the hotel and THEN make over 100 mattresses for them! Well, they then gave me some 'song and dance' about how there wasn't a warehouse that held the mattresses and that they did in fact make the mattresses upon request from each region and that Jamison was going to continue to make their mattresses up until a certain time so it was indeed the same mattress. This sounded suspicious but they already had my money and they kept assuring me that this would be the same mattress so I waited.

I think you know where I'm going with this.

I eventually got my mattress. I put the mattress pad on it. The tag said that it came from Jamison and although it didn't have the same model number on it, the name of the mattress line was the same. Because it's new, when I laid on it I could tell that it was comfortable but I couldn't tell if it was the same one because obviously the hotel mattresses have been slept on for a longer time and were therefore broken in while this one was not.

However, it is now a year later and even though this mattress has been slept on by 2 people every night for 6 months and it still does not feel like the Jamison mattresses that I have slept on when I stayed in Marriott hotels!!

Is it comfortable? It's okay.

Would I have spent $2000 on it? No.

Do I think that they are running a scam at this point? Yes. I think that they didn't bank on the Jamison company selling out to another company and changing the way they've made mattresses. I think that Marriott has made a lot of money off of the mattresses that Jamison has provided them and while they are trying to figure out what other mattresses they're going to use (I heard that they are using Serta mattresses now) they are trying to ride on their previous reputation for having comfortable beds in order to sell the other mattress models that Jamison makes but that the Marriott company never felt were actually comfortable enough to use for their hotels!

If you're calling the Marriott number anytime after December 2014 and you speak to a customer service representative, keep in mind that they're going to tell you exactly what was written on their scripts to tell you! They don't really know what it is they are selling you because they are off-site OR they know that they're selling you a Jamison mattress but they know that it's not the same mattresses that the Marriott has purchased from Jamison in the past. The bottom line is that the Marriott Jamison mattress line has fallen and is honestly no longer available to the public.Good luck!attresses that Jamison has provided them and while they are trying to figure out what other mattresses they're going to use (I heard that they are using Serta mattresses now) they are trying to ride on their previous reputation for having comfortable beds in order to sell the other mattress models that Jamison makes but that the Marriott company never felt were actually comfortable enough to use for their hotels!

If you're calling the Marriott number anytime after December 2014 and you speak to a customer service representative, keep in mind that they're going to tell you exactly what was written on their scripts to tell you! They don't really know what it is they are selling you because they are off-site OR they know that they're selling you a Jamison mattress but they know that it's not the same mattresses that the Marriott has purchased from Jamison in the past. The bottom line is that the Marriott Jamison mattress line has fallen and is honestly no longer available to the public.Good luck!

review_headline: Sturdy enough, but poor finish quality and packaging.
review_body:

These shelves are particle board as would be expected. The veneer is so thin that you can see the particle board texture through the veneer. The veneer of two of the shelves was damaged upon receipt. Having said that, the shelves are remarkably sturdy for what they are. The documentation states that each shelf can support fifteen pounds between each set of support poles. Assembly was trivial and consists of screwing the plastic poles together with the shelving in between. I would recommend following the directions in reverse order. Screw the flat tops on first and work your way down to the feet. If you work from the bottom up, you will find that you are unable to tighten the flat caps on top when you are done!

I would NOT recommend this product for an area often visited by guests due to it's poor finish quality. I would recommend it for something like a craft or dorm room.

review_body: Here are a few observations after just assembling this patio set:  Assembly: Took two people 90 minutes to unbox and completely assemble. No additional screws are included. It is best to loosely tighten the screws before going through and fully tightening, as the holes can be difficult to line up - this will save a big headache. Strength: Two people weighing a combined 350+ pounds were able to sit on the couch without it wobbling or bending. The chairs are also sturdy, and a 6' 1" 200+ pound man was able to sit comfortably. This is impressive, as each piece is very light weight. One person can easily lift the couch.  Overall, this set seems to be a bargain at this price. If you are looking for a simple, relatively compact patio set that looks nice, you have found it.  EDIT 7/13/16 I am updating after the first winter with this set. The furniture was left outdoors all season to endure near 0 degrees Fahrenheit temperatures, snow, hail and sleet. So far, there is absolutely no visible damage of any kind to the chairs, loveseat, table or glass. I did not keep the cushions outside through the winter.  EDIT 9/26/16 The front facing material of the back support has separated from the loveseat's frame. The couch was in the sun nearly all summer, but this set was sold as "weather resistant." I have lowered the review to three stars, as the two chairs and table are still flawless.

review_body:
I have wanted one of these for some time now, and I am very satisfied with my purchase. I refer to it as my nest, and my cats think it also belongs to them. The bean bag came in the shipping box, with plastic wrapped tightly around the tan fabric casing that contained the foam inside. I pulled away the plastic around the beanbag, and it was already starting to poof out. I let it go for an hour or two, and then put the cover on it (very nice cover by the way). Then I turned and kneaded at it - repeatedly/alternating - and then settled on it a few times. The cover does not attract/hold a lot of pet hair as I had feared. I have slept on it two nights in a row, my cats love it and frequently claim it as their own, and my sofa has been neglected. My only recommendation is that you make sure your rotate and fluff it frequently (based on how much you sit in it). The foam can settle a bit when you sit in the same spot on it for hours on end, so just give it some fluff.

It is very large, like a twin bed. If you don't want something that big, I recommend one of the smaller versions. I included a picture with this review, and hope it helps you to get a good idea of the size (excuse the mess, I just moved). review_headline: I will buy a million of these...
review_body:
Yes. Any time I could ever need a bed, I will buy one of these for the rest of my life. It is so affordable, and so ridiculously comfortable, I want to cry thinking about money I have spent on other beds. I used to feel bad for making my professional boyfriend sleep on my mattress on the floor in my tiny student apartment - turns out, he likes my bed better than he likes his! Maybe this will be an early birthday present for him. And I could even afford it!

It is soft and has the body-cradling attributes of memory foam, but also has a "push-back" factor that keeps it from being a back-tweaker. The smell dissipated quickly, and I use the Sleep Defense System Mattress Encasement with it because I have an unholy terror of bedbugs. This makes it sleep hot, and I can say less about the hot/cold factor because of that. Either way I would recommend a mattress pad and a frame or boxspring. From what I can tell it is "unidirectional" - you can't flip it upside down and get the same feeling, but thats just based on the pattern.

Overall this was just a total Amazon score and I am very delighted with it.

product_title: Signature Sleep Premium Ultra Steel Foundation Mattresses
review_body: I had high hopes for this steel foundation. My husband and I are both large, tall people, and the cheap wooden foundations we have had in the past would never hold up and just splinter into a thousand pieces. We had just purchased a new foam mattress, and wanted a new, nice foundation to go with it. After researching several options, we settled on the Signature Sleep Premium Ultra Steel Foundation. We will go ahead and knock off one star for the headache of putting this thing together. It comes in about a million pieces, all taped and zip tied together, so, just getting everything unpacked took forever. I am usually the person who builds new items in our household, so I had no reservations about getting started. Although I succeeded in my mission, I would not recommend building this yourself. The people who claimed it went together easily in a short time are obviously octopus mutant humanoids. However, I honestly would have been fine with the difficult build had I ended up with a foundation that was worth it. Let's take away the second star for the noise. One of the main reasons I purchased this frame was because of all the positive reviews about how quiet this bed was. We have a steel frame, as well, that has never made a sound. I am a light sleeper and a quiet bed is important to me. Unfortunately, this bed is anything but quiet. It squeaks if you look at it too hard. Loudly. Because I did have some difficulty getting it together, I went back through with my husband and made sure everything was tightened properly (with a new allen wrench, as the one it came with was useless long before the project was finished) and it is still super squeaky. My last complaint is probably tied up with the squeaky issue, but I am taking a star, anyway. The screws are cheap and they do need tightened once a month or so. The bed squeaks regardless, but gets much worse when it is time to go back through and tighten everything up. I will say the foundation is very sturdy when tightened,it looks nice, and I like the height of it. However, I would not purchase this item again.

product_title: 128gb Micro Sd Hc Card with Free Adapter 10 Class Universal Tf Flash Memory Card
review_headline: SDHC is valid to a 32GB and NO MORE
review_body:
If you even see an "SDHC" (not "SDXC") card advertising 64GB or more, look elsewhere. You could lose some or all of your valuable data If you buy this card.

Beware of fake capacity SD memory cards. This and many other cheap, apparently-high-capacity SD memory cards are often low capacity 8GB or 16GB cards that have been hacked (controller chip settings altered) by dishonest Chinese suppliers so that they show a false inflated capacity. That is why their price is so low. These cards are then redistributed by many clueless resellers and by many other fully-aware resellers who are out to make a quick profit.

Such cards will show their false capacity both in your phone and in Windows properties, and they will even work normally under low usage. However, once their true (low) capacity is exceeded, they will quietly lose or corrupt your valuable data. Files will look okay in their folders, but will be corrupt when viewed, played, or otherwise read back. Your photos, videos, music, contact list, and other data will be irretrievably lost.

Be especially wary of cards with a stated capacity of 64GB or above marked as "SDHC" (not "SDXC"). The SD card association controls and licenses the SD card standards and they define "SDHC" up to a maximum capacity of 32GB. For larger capacity cards, only the "SDXC" standard is valid.

Good 128GB SD cards are out there, but they will conform to the SDXC standard and will be clearly marked as such. Expect to pay roughly $25 and up for 64GB (as of Q2 2015) and at least twice that for 128GB cards.

If you do buy a low-priced card, the first thing you should do is test the capacity using a utility called h2testw. This will fill the card with data and then verify that it can be read back intact. The write phase usually completes without error. It is the verify phase that exposes the fake capacity. Testing the first 32GB is usually sufficient.

You can also test by filling the card up to at least 30% with videos or other large media files and then *most importantly* check to see if they can be played back. If the capacity is faked, the first few will play, but past some point, the rest will be corrupt.

Search for "fake capacity flash" using your favorite search engine for more information.br />

product_title: Home Styles Crescent Hill Pantry
review_headline: Not worth the money or the hassle
review_body:
Pros: This item was delivered on time. It arrived in two large boxes and each item was protected from damage. All but one needed part were in the boxes. The pieces are heavy for ready to assemble furniture. The finish was as described and pictured.

Cons: There are a number of problems with the piece that was shipped to us. In Box 1, a support piece had detached from the piece. Six wood screws were loose in the box. The piece was easy to reattach, but all of the base parts were quite loose and needed significant tightening. One of the legs is missing the plastic bottom piece (the part that comes between the furniture and the floor) so if assembled as is it would rock quite a bit.

Box 2 contained the most problems. Three of the four doors are damaged. One door has a small, but noticeable gouge on the front. The two bottom doors have large swirling, whitish lines on the inside. I assume they were created by machinery. The top and middle pieces have perfectly straight scratched lines on the front. The top piece also has a noticeable chip on one side. The drawer front has a crack that appears to have an attempt at a repair.

We called the company and were told there was no way a pantry would have this much damage. They asked for pictures, which we provided. It has been two weeks and we are still trying to get the company to fix the problem. Either we happened to get a lemon of a pantry or this company needs to work on their quality control.

review_headline: I find this chair quite comfortable. Pros
review_body:
I'm 5'10", 170lbs and reasonably fit. I find this chair quite comfortable.

Pros:
- It was a snap to put together and includes all the tools you'll need.
- The chair sits evenly and and makes little to no noise when I move around
- Can be reclined 170 degrees and without a running start you couldn't tip this thing over.
- Holds you tightly in an upright position and has relieved a good portion of back pain.
- Included pillows are quality and ad options to your comfort.
- Arm rests can be removed without sacrificing any other functionality for all you guitar players out there.

Con:
- The included pillows don't attach how the pictures indicate. Specifically the back support has two elastic bands with plastic clips that run up and down the back portion of the chair. It's kind of an eye sore.

Thoughts:
- Check your BMI and reference the manufacturer website to see what they recommend for you. This chair is designed to hold you in an upright position and it will do exactly that. My BMI is 24.4 if you are much larger than that or have a large bottom end you should consider a different model.

The box this comes in actually kind of small for a chair but don’t let the size fool you, it’s heavy! Once you take everything out of the box, putting it together is pretty straight forward. It comes with the one tool you need. Following the instructions it took me less than 25 minutes to put the chair together. (I was watching Big Bang Theory at the time so it would probably take less time without the distraction.)

The high back is a great feature for me. I’ve found if I have a mid to low back chair I don’t lean back in it which in the short term, it’s fine. But long term my back starts to feel the stress of me trying to sit up straight. This chair offers both options. I can sit straight and when I want to relax to say watch a video, I lean back and let the chair support me. It was comfortable for the few hours I spend sitting.

At the current price of $224.90, it is too high for this quality with other less pricey options available with equal quality.

product_title: Crosley Furniture Rolling Kitchen Island
review_body:
This is a nice island in general, and an okay island for the price. The instructions were not very clear, so some of the pieces are backwards (there are a few metal parts showing) but it's not a big deal, and the customer support helped me figure out how to get it together in terms of making the pieces fit (I have assembled a lot of flat-pack furniture, and these instructions were lacking).

Anyway, the other reviews that said it takes an hour to verify all the pieces are there: correct, there are a lot of pieces and it's crucial to ensure they are all there; the ones saying it smells: yes, it does have a short (1 week or so) period following unpacking in which there is off-gassing, and even now the scent is noticeable but subtly there; the reviews complaining the packaging was not good: some of the pieces were chipped, but nothing that was structurally significant or visually obtrusive (turn the damaged parts around and it looks fine).

So overall, it took me a while to get this together, but the hex wrench included was among the better hex wrenches I've seen in flat-pack furniture. I really like the side racks for small items, and the other is great for paper towels.

I wanted the stainless steel top for heat & looks and it is great for both, but since it's polished, it shows marks after it's been cleaned (streak marks). So maybe the wood top is better; it's definitely cheaper.

The white cart is not laminated as I feared it might be, but looks like painted wood (except the two back panels, but it's not a huge deal).

So, overall...not great in terms of what you get for the price. It's a good piece!! But worth a little less. And the instructions can be tricky. And it's not perfect. But it has added a lot of storage room to our kitchen. So it's probably one of the best you will find on Amazon. I would kind of recommend it.

product_title: Cabot L Shaped Desk
review_headline: Not especially pleased. Bad for gaming PCs.
review_body:
PROS:
It's easy enough to assemble.
It looks nice. The glass cabinet door is quite elegant.

CONS:
The instructions could be a little more clear; the orientation of some of the more complicated pieces was hard to see.
The holes for the track of the file drawer were not correctly aligned, so it sticks out about an inch from the front of the desk.
The charging station is a weird felted cardboard thing that is (barely) held together with Velcro. It just sits in the opening and is prone to tipping backwards.
The little alcove really should have been a drawer. I have no idea why there isn't one there, except maybe to keep the cost down. It's pretty much wasted space.
The cabinet allows for no air circulation to your computer. NONE! That's fine for a small PC running easy programs. if you play games DO NOT PUT YOUR PC IN THE CABINET! Even with the door open, all of the hot air will accumulate in the back and it will still overheat.

OVERALL:
It's a sturdy desk with a nice amount of space for working. Not good for a gaming PC unless you plan to modify it.

There are a few things that keep this from being a 5 star product:

Again, not a huge deal, but I am probably going to have to paint it at some point. Finally, the stainless top is a pretty low grade of stainless and scratches very badly. For us, this is a working island, so we aren't too concerned with the scratches, but I think it is unfortunate, especially given the cost of the piece. Which brings me to the cost. Amazon's price was the best I found. If I had paid the full price on this, I would have been very disappointed with the poor quality steel. As it is, we are happy with the island. product_title: LUCID 10 Inch Gel Memory Foam Mattress - Dual-Layered - CertiPUR-US Certified - 25-Year Warranty
review_headline: FIVE STARS TO ONE.  Back pain and sleeping problems within 1 YEAR.
review_body: UPDATE!  FROM FIVE STARS TO ONE!  One year later -  we purchased the mattress on February 25, 2015, and received it about two weeks later (Fulfillment by Amazon had an issue and forgot to mail it to us).  It has now been just barely over one year since we started sleeping on the mattress, and now WE HAVE HAD TO REPLACE IT.  For the last few month we have noticed the comfort level dropping off, and problems with our sleep creeping into our lives.  Now the only comfortable places on the mattress are within 8" of the edge, as the center of the mattress has a divit about 4" deep, 5' long and 4' wide that no longer provides any support.  My wife and I are both of average height and weight, and we did not use the mattress for anything outside of the norm for any normal couple, ie we didn't jump up and down on the bed, we didn't leave the microwave on it for an extended period, etc etc etc.  We had the bed supported by normal, purpose designed bed slats (ikea bed, all the normal framing and support)  What we noticed with the mattress was that while our hips and center of weight would push down on the middle of the mattress, our extremities would put less stress on the outer regions of the mattress, creating a disproportion of stress.  Thus, one year later the middle of the mattress where we sleep next to each other sags a massive 4" while our heads and feet are being supported at the normal height.  Even after a recent 1 week vacation, the mattress did not return to its original height.  The discomfort and sleeping problems this caused for us became so extreme that we could no longer use the mattress and have replaced it.    Trying to find info on how to make a warranty claim, but you cannot contact the seller with it being FBA, and the warranty card has ZERO PHONE NUMBER OR CONTACT INFO ON IT.

review_headline: ... Once you put all the pieces together it's a pretty nice looking piece of furniture
review_body:
Pros -
Once you put all the pieces together it's a pretty nice looking piece of furniture.
I searched the entire internet and my local stores as well and in my opinion the price can't be beat when you consider the quality of this product.

Cons -
Overengineering! You will spend HOURS putting any South Shore product together.
In my opinion this company needs to understand that some people are buying their products for children so it would be nice if they rounded their corners. I just re-modeled my daughters room with this bookshelf, dresser, computer desk and a nightstand and every single piece of furniture has sharp edges and they are unforgiving if you accidentally brush up against them.
Although the price is very reasonable I do NOT expect to chip any part of this item while putting it together. They really need to charge a little more and fix that problem.

Overall, I would recommend this product to a friend, but I would warn them with the cons that I mentioned above.

review_body:
These are really nice looking and heavy-duty chairs-- but I ordered two and had problems with both of them. First off, you have to unscrew the seat pads to take off the plastic wrap that's around the pads. When I tried to screw the seat pads back in, I noticed that one of the screw holes was stripped. Not a huge deal (I hope) because there are three other screws.

But the bigger problem was the bolts that attach the legs to the chair... they didn't line up correctly on either chair. On one chair, I was finally able to just muscle my way through and force the final bolt in even though it's crooked. On the other, it's impossible-- it's not even close to lined up. So I have one chair with three bolts instead of four holding the legs on, and I'm not sure how safe that is over time. I'm considering having a handyman drill a new hole and maybe glue it in place. One of the drawbacks to buying furniture online, of course, is the issue of returns... I'm frazzled thinking about disassembling them and trying to fit them back into their boxes, ship them back, and wait for replacements that might or might not have the same issue. But these are nicer chairs than anything I found in person, which is why I took the chance and bought them online.

Aside from those problems: The memory return works well, the finish is accurately pictured and appears more bronze than pewter (doesn't look great against my stainless steel appliances, but is an elegant finish nonetheless), and has a pleasing overall shape and design. Seat pads are comfortable and the chairs feel substantial, like they're made to last-- aside from the bolt/screw issues!

Update: PlumStruck was responsive and easy to work with on offering either a partial refund or full return and replacement.

I bought this exact DHP mattress and used it with a steel platform bed-frame. Its been 5 years later and this mattress is still very comfortable and held up well. It is very thick and heavy, and comes in vacuum-sealed plastic, tightly rolled up in a disposable duffle bag. Once you free it from the plastic, it immediantly begins "inhaling" air and puffing up to full-size, as well as the coil-springs expanding. It did have a musty smell at first but that went away after the first few days.

The only downside is that because its so big, getting it back into its packaging is impossible if you want to return it. UPS won't take it unless it is in an actual box. You probably won't want to return it though, as it is a very nice and comfortable mattress.

Highly recommended. If you're looking for an inexpensive, quality bed option, then this full-size mattress along with a full-size steel platform bed frame, should cost no more than $250.

product_title: King's Brand 2950 Glass and Metal Home Office Computer Workstation Desk/Table, Silver Finish
review_headline: Low keyboard tray and glass fibers.
review_body:
The desk itself is fine, sturdy and attractive.

Packaging is excellent, very heavy duty cardboard; little risk of the glass being broken on arrival.

Like other reviewers have said, there appear to be little glass fibers everywhere inside the packaging, every piece was covered in them. Use a Swiffer and vacuum promptly after opening, you don't want these flying around your house.

Assembly is straightforward for anyone who can assemble ikea-style furniture. Only nitpick is the keyboard tray was not pre-drilled or tapped, had to break out the electric drill and template the pilot holes. The included self-tapping screws were nearly impossible to do by hand (I did one without the drill and gave up).

My biggest complaint about this desk is about the keyboard tray. While it is plenty wide (wide enough for a fullsize keyboard + ample room for a mouse) it is really low. I'm 6'-0" tall, and with my chair at the proper height the tray just barely clears the top of thighs, and is nowhere near the right height for ergonomic keyboard use. In fact, my chair will not adjust any lower, so I will likely place some risers underneath the feet to add another 2" of height.

product_title: Best Price Mattress Tri-Fold Memory Foam Mattress Topper, 4-Inch
review_headline: Too big to pack for camping, but perfect for glamping
review_body:
This mattress is pretty firm and comfortable, but like other reviews have pointed out, it very narrow and long when it's opened up. It'd be great to put on top of uncomfortable futons or cots, or just to use as a makeshift bed on the floor. It's really lightweight and the boxy shape makes it easy to take in and out of storage.

I thought that it would be great for camping, but it takes up a lot of room even when it's stowed away in the carrying case. It would be, by far, the largest piece of equipment that I would pack for a camping trip. When stored in the case, the broad side is about 34 x 25.5 inches, and it's 13 inches deep. That makes it about the size of a 40" flat screen TV and several times thicker.

This mattress would great for long roadtrips or cabin strips if you have the room in your car for something that's about the size of a medium-sized flat screen TV box. It's pretty comfortable, and I'm a little disappointed that I won't have the room in my car to take it camping, but I'll keep it around for guests and trips where I might have the room in my car.

review_headline: Prefect fix for wood stairs and dogs

These are great in that they are durable, easy to clean and have a rubberish backing that doesn't slide as much as you'd think without using double sided tape (which I am hesitant to do on wood floors).  I can remove them when cleaning the stairs or to shake out and vacuum when they get riddled with pet hair. You could use tape though or rubber carpet stickies if you have young children that you worry will slip, or very large dogs that might knock them constantly out of place; my 35 lb dogs don't. They are more of a taupe color than what is pictured on the sellers photo, or perhaps it's just that the floor color on Amazons picture is a more orange toned.  Overall I am very happy with these runners, and they were priced higher on other websites.  I included photos taken with natural daylight as well as my foyer lighting to show the color as accurately as possible.

review_body:
We are really enjoying this ottoman so far. It is the perfect size for our large sectional sofa, and the lift top works nice for the family "picnic" in front of the TV. I was honestly scared to order this based on earlier reviews of items damaged in shipment, but with the sparse number of items available at this size we decided to roll the dice.

The good:
- Its large size is perfect for us and it also provides a bunch of storage that we have yet to fill up.
- This top is soft, but firm. It's comfortable to sit on or prop feet on, but firm enough to put a glass on without worrying about it falling over.
- It shipped quickly and arrived fast

The not-so-good:
- The stitching in the middle of each top section doesn't line up. To me this shows lack of attention to detail in manufacturing and cost one star on this review.
- The packaging for shipment was inadequate, and I can see why so many people have received damaged pieces. Ours arrived in a banged-up box, but escaped any noticeable damage.

I would recommend this to a friend, but would still expect a 50/50 chance of receiving a damaged unit unless they improve the packaging.

product_title: Bags for Less Folding Chair in a Bag Black/ Grey
review_headline: The best folding chair I've ever had. Even has padding inside!
review_body:
Okay so this...this is one awesome folding chair. This is not that cheap chair you pick up from a display at the check out of your local hardware store. I have a whole bunch of those. No, this one is so much better.

I have a lot of these kinds of chairs, all different quality levels. During the summer, my teen daughter plays soft ball on a city team. Between practices and games, I spend 4 out of every 7 days sitting in one of these types of chairs. I need a folding chair because frequently I am walking a distance between the parking lot and the ball field. So I need something that folds up and can be carried in a bag. However most folding chairs like these are just okay. The nylon is usually pretty thin and they're about as comfortable as anything would be that's holding you up by a few metal legs. But this one...this one is different.

First, the size is bigger. Some chairs if you're taller than 5'5" feet, you feel like the chair is too small for you. Not this one. It a real grown up chair. My 6' tall hubby can sit in this and not have his knees up around his ears.

And second, the best feature. It's padded! Yes, padded. It's not just one layer of nylon like all the other chairs out there. This one is two layers, with a thin layer of padding in-between them. And to keep the padding in place, the material has subtle quilting seams sewn in. It's not only a larger chair, but it's actually got some substance to the materiel, making sitting in it for hours on end so much nicer.

And third, it can keep you warmer. It doesn't make you hot to sit in it, but something I always run into is when at some of the ball games early in the season, I get cold. Especially since they always play back-to-back softball games, so by the end of the second one, the sun is starting to set. And in May in Minnesota, it's still chilly, especially in the evening and when by one of the lakes.

In my other folding chairs, I get cold quick. The thin nylon doesn't do anything for keeping your back side warm at all, especially when the wind is blowing. One could stay warmer in a metal folding chair. But this chair I can stay warm in. The double layer of nylon material combined with the thin quilted padding inside help block cold winds from making your backside cold. I love it.

The chair comes with a large nylon carrying case and there is a drink holder built into the arm rest. The frame easily holds my husbands 200+ lb 6 foot tall frame. This is by far the best folding chair we've ever used. I want 3 more of them!

product_title: Mid Back Mesh Ergonomic Computer Desk Office Chair
review_headline: You get what you pay for.
review_body:
This chair is good enough for the price (I got it cheaper from a private seller). It's relatively straightforward to put together, but they neglect to tell you (as another reviewer mentioned) that you should NOT screw the arms in all the way before putting the back on. That part was a huge pain to discover, and even compressing the arms, I had a hard time getting the screws in. It's all together now, but it was a pain. If you have a rope, I suggest pulling it out to use for compression if necessary.

It's not tall enough for my desk, but I think my desk may be unusually tall (it's in a loft bed). But it'll do; I can always add a cushion. It does also feel small; the seat could be a bit wider, and the arms touch my thighs easily. Luckily, I'm small, so it's not a big deal, but if that worries you, I would try a different chair.

It's comfortable; the back is supportive enough for me, the seat isn't overly soft, but not painful either. It rolls nicely. It raises and lowers smoothly. Can't really complain all that much.

If you order this and your shipment shows as Delivered on Amazon, but you only get one box, **contact Amazon immediately.** Our first shipment only arrived with the metal pieces, no wood, and was marked as Delivered. After some discussion with customer service, they sent me a whole new shipment-- not with two-day Prime shipping this time for some reason, but it did at least all arrive..

There's inconsistent staining (in places that aren't as noticeable though so it's not a deal breaker). For example, on the legs of the Vanity. The staining looks good from the top looking down but if you were to look from the bottom there are parts where the staining didn't get a good cover. One of the legs does not screw in all the way so it wobbles. Lucky for me this is going on carpet and it's a little more forgiving on this issue. If this were going on a hard surface then it would have been returned that same day. If i need to move it in the future then i guess i'll need to get crafty.

The stool has a similar issue with one of the legs but I was able to fix this by just gluing the leg to the base of the seat. I can't foresee any reason I would ever need to remove the legs of the stool so it didn't seem to matter.

There were multiple other little issues that i fixed along the way but i'm writing this review awhile after I bought this so i unfortunately don't remember them.

All in all I didn't have any issues that made me want to box this thing back up and send it back. That would have been a real pain. Not worth the effort. If I had the opportunity though, I would not buy this again.

Then, of course, I expected that it would take an hour to assemble and that it would become structurally less stable every time it was moved to clean around it ... The veneer is an attractive gray and seems quite tough. Don't get me wrong, this is budget furniture, there's no solid wood here. But, it's just what I needed and I'm very happy I took a gamble on buying from this line of furniture on the net. Two thumbs up. product_title: kathy ireland Office by Bush Furniture New York Skyline 60-Inch L-Desk with Glass Return, Plumeria White
review_headline: Pleased but with a few suggestions
review_body:
First I want to thank those that answered a question I had about this desk before ordering. It arrived today and came well packaged. Be prepared for styrofoam galore. There are two boxes and both weight quite a bit. I am unsure how the Fed Ex guy would have unloaded both boxes by himself as it took both my husband and teenage son to bring the boxes into the house. I am glad Fed Ex came later in the afternoon after my husband came home otherwise I am suspecting the boxes would have been dragged to the porch. I don't see how handling these boxes in a one person job.

Assembly took my husband about two hours. We had one snag as one of the main pieces has pre-glued wooden dowels. One of the dowels was snapped clean off leaving the the rest firmly stuck in the hole. Since we have built tons of IKEA furniture, we have spare parts we keep just in case. We ended up needed that extra dowel. My husband had to drill out the dowel that was stuck in the hole and replace with one of our spare parts. The rest of the assembly went fairly well.

The end result is a very nice looking desk. It is very sturdy and I like the feel of the finish. The crystal drawer handles are a nice touch. The drawers themselves feel a bit too snug and don't roll as smoothly as I had hoped. The drawers do not line up perfectly but I have a critical eye, the slight misalignment does not affect the function. I want to mention that the two top drawers have a felt lining in them. I didn't see this in the description so that was an nice touch. Unfortunately my husband didn't notice at first so we had to take the drawers apart and flip the bottom around. Be sure to flip all 3 drawer bottoms over to find the felt pieces before drawer assembly.

I actually don't find the USB hub that useful as I am unsure of where to plug the end into. I suppose I could thread the cord back up through the desk and plug into the computer but unsure of how that would look. If I am missing something here, I am all ears. I agree a power strip would have been a better feature. There are some plastic hanger pieces that help with cord management. These screw underneath the desk. I only found one hole that one of the cord management brackets screw into and it looks like that is all I need so that works out for me.

My overall thoughts of the desk is that it is attractive and going to function well for me. The glass on the return is an interesting touch but I don't find it very useful. The shelf underneath the glass is nice for placing a notebook or two. I would have preferred the white top to continue on the return portion. Although I understood the measurements of the desk, I am more of a visible person and after getting the desk together, the return is rather short. I think it makes the desk feel a little crowded so if I could change the layout, I would have preferred the return to be longer in length and have a second set of drawers on the end. The main portion of the desk is nice and wide but it is not very deep. My plan was to put my iMac in the center and run the power cord through the hole in the desk but since the depth is not as much as I had hoped, this left little room for the keyboard. I ended up putting the computer on angle toward the end of the desk, since it is placed against one wall, running the cord behind the desk worked out. I am pleased with the desk, with a few tweaks I mentioned above, the desk would be absolutely perfect.

review_headline: They really will work if you follow these directions!
review_body: We bought these to use with the king size Pragma bedframe after we purchased a new Tuft and Needle mattress. I purchased 2 sets so I could attach both a headboard and footboard. When I first tried to install the footboard I had a moment of panic--as other reviewers have noted, it seemed the footboard was too wide for the holes in the brackets. But after looking carefully at the brackets I figured out how to solve the problem. The holes on the top of the brackets are oblong to allow slight repositioning. So I did the following: 1) completely removed the screws holding the bracket on the side of the bedframe; 2) then loosened the screws at the end of the bedframe just enough so I could slide them farther out to accomodate the footboard. 3) Next I bolted the footboard to the brackets, 4) I then was able to tighten the end screws back down. 5) The brackets are somewhat flexible so I was able to push them into place to reinsert the side screws and tighten them down. I did the headboard the same way and it fits perfectly. We now have a beautiful bed with 14" of storage underneath! (Oh, and the bed frame is great, too!)

product_title: Z-Line Designs Feliz Glass L Desk, Black
review_headline: Well, it looked nice on paper
review_body:
This was a Christmas gift from my mother. I was pretty excited, since my previous glass corner desk was starting to fall apart after being in constant use for 8 years. This seemed to be a great upgrade, with better supports and nicer welds and generally better detail. However, it wasn't all rosy when I began assembling it.

After clearing out space for this desk, I began unpacking it. Just like everyone else, I was appalled by the poor packaging. It is cheap, garbage styrofoam that WILL get all over the place. I vacuumed the room at least four times during and after the setup process. It flakes easily and it snaps in half with no effort, making your immediate surroundings look like a winter wonderland.

The setup process is rather simple and can be done very quickly by one person. It took me under 20 minutes to set the desk frame up with no issues. I was pleased with the construction and the differences in the frame compared to my old desk. I even remarked that I thought it would probably last as long as the last one or even longer.

The problems began when I unpacked the glass. I don't know who thought it was a good idea to use stickers designed for cardboard boxes on the glass, but I'd love to find out so I can call them an idiot. The stickers to not remove cleanly from the glass. They will rip and peel and leave you frustrated. Nothing short of a flat razor blade would get these stickers off cleanly. Even after that, I had to polish off the remaining sticky residue with Windex. This is glass. Use glass stickers. Removing the stickers cleanly took me twice as long as setting up the frame... 40 minutes.

Then things got worse. I pushed the desk into place up against the wall. It would be silly to try and move it with the heavy glass on it. Once it was in place, I put on the smaller pieces of glass. The corner piece and keyboard piece fit perfectly into place. The small shelf was a bit off, but I continued anyway. I put the big glass piece on the keyboard side, and it did not fit correctly. I thought it was odd, but I put on the other one just to be sure. That one didn't fit either. I switched them around. Same thing. The glass did not match the angles of the desk. When I could get it to line up on one side, the other side would be an inch or more forward or back to the front of the frame.

I tried adjusting the way the frame was sitting, thinking that perhaps the carpet in the room was making the frame get out of alignment. No change in the glass. I measured the glass. Same size and dimensions. I then thought to check the frame. I measured the screw holes on the frame, and they seem to have been drilled at a slight angle.

Ok, follow me on this one. If you have this desk, you can follow along, if not, refer to the pictures. There are two support rods that go under the glass on each side. Each side has two large support legs that go down to the floor. The support rods do not make a perfect 90 degree angle to the support legs. They are off by right about 7 or 8 degrees, which is keeping the glass from sitting perfectly into place.

I did some measurements and found that the screw opening on one single support leg is drilled at a slight angle. It measures 2.55" from the front on one side and 2.48" on the other side. This is why the glass won't fit properly. It is forcing the support rods to be at an angle. There is no way this is going to fit properly ever.

To make matters worse, the glass does not fit the area of the frame. It is about 1" deeper than the frame, so it is going to stick out either in the front or the back, your choice. I have no idea why it is like this.

I'm going to be contacting the seller to take this thing back, but due to the awful packaging, there is no possibility of repackaging this thing without causing further damage to it.

Maybe I just got a lemon. I don't really know. The other reviews are praising this desk like it's the second coming, so I guess it is possible that my situation is a one-off thing. Who knows, really? In any case, this manufacturer certainly has a lot of room for improvements.

product_title: Simpli Home Acadian TV Stand
review_body:
Nice, as in "I like you, you're nice." Not "wow, I'm liking you baby. Nice." Overall, shoddy. To be fair, the piece is sturdy mainly due to the H-shaped drawer assembly.
There are two sets of door handles but the screws are of different length, so it's easy and perhaps inevitable you will get these mixed up.

Assembled by myself in about three hours (about an hour too long in my opinion). Two people are recommended and putting the two sides on appears to be where another human would come in handy.

The back panels use screws instead of nails, which I was happy about. However, out of four panels there were five drilled holes, most in a single panel. This led to an errant screw coming through the wood at an angle and breaking out a chunk of the interior. If this isn't particle board, it might as well be.

The hex wrench provided in the kit, to be blunt, is junk. If you don't have a set of hex wrenches, this is a good excuse to buy one.

Given the choice again, I would not have bought this item. An item by the same maker at the same size -- but without the glass doors -- costs half as much. This means each glass door effectively costs $100. Are hinges really that expensive?

Item does not offer much scratch resistance. Supports the weight of an 80-pound TV without issue. Would not recommend with a gun to my head.

review_headline: DO NOT get this mattress.  Owned it for over a year and now I have serious back issues.
review_body:
I bought this mattress about a year ago after seeing all the positive reviews on Amazon. At first it was great and refreshing to be sleeping on a nice firm mattress, but after 3 or 4 months, that firmness disappears. I have a huge sink hole in the middle of the mattress. If I lay on the sides and roll into the middle its almost like hopping on an elevator and going down a floor. One morning about 5 months ago I woke up with a back pain to the point I couldn't even turn around. After about a week of having this pain, one of my discs herniated in my spine and that was the most painful experience in my life. After herniating my disc, I had to move all the way to the edge of my bed to sleep because of the pain my back was in.

I bought this mattress in hopes of it helping my back but it instead ended up causing me a life long issue. DO NOT buy this mattress unless you plan on sleeping in a completely different spot every night so you won't end up getting a huge dip.

product_title: Cheetah Mounts ALAMB Articulating Arm (15” Extension) TV Wall Mount Bracket for 12-24” TVs and Displays up to VESA 100 and up to 40lbs, Including a 10’ Twisted Veins HDMI Cable
review_headline: this will work just fine, and it is a real bargain - Revised
review_body: See Revision, below!    An OK mount, but it is difficult to get it adjusted to move smoothly when you want it to, but not when you don't.  If you want to mount a monitor to the wall and never move it, this will work just fine, and it is a real bargain, but if you want to move it around...    I have a small (32\\") flat screen, weighs maybe 7#.  I have the mount properly mounted to a wood bookcase, but rotate & fold it out and around when I want to actually watch TV.  So, when it is stored, the TV is in Portrait mode, when I'm watching it, it is in Landscape mode.    If I loosen the mount up to allow smooth rotation, then when I store it away, over the course of a day, the weight of the TV makes it angle down ( like this \ versus | ).  And, the swing arm also moves the TV away from the bookcase.  So, instead of having the TV neatly stored away beside the bookcase, 3 inches +/-, and straight up & down, it creeps out and angles, so it is more like 7 inches away at the top, and 3 inches at the bottom.    Normally, I wouldn't care, but this is in my \\"formal\\" living room, and I tried to make the TV as inconspicuous as possible when it isn't in use.  If I had to do again, I would have likely bought one with either separate tilt vs. rotation tension adjustments, or one with a thumbscrew adjustment (vs. an hex head screw).    REVISED - added TWO Stars....  Shortly after I posted the 3-star rating of the unit, I got both an Email and Phone call from Cheetah.  They wanted to know what was wrong, and what could be done better.  I told them what I said in the review, and they understood.  They then recommended a larger mount, even though my TV was far less than the 40# rated limit of the original mount.  A few days later, I had a much beefier mount, with the same *basic* design, but, it has a swivel ball that is a different material (softer? stickier?).    The new mount used the exact same holes that the old one used, which was good, since I was mounting it on the side of a bookcase.  I mounted it on Sunday, and tightened it up to that the TV both rotated & tilted smoothly.  However, due to the different swivel ball material, it hasn't moved at all since then.  Which is what I was hoping for.    The new mount is this: \\"Cheetah Articulating Arm TV Wall Mount 23-Inch to 49-Inch, 20-Inch Extension\\" (ASIN: B001GTT0VO), which is only a little bit more money than the original mount.  I should have purchased that one to begin with, but Cheetah was kind enough to correct my mistake.    They have also tried to reach me a couple of times since Sunday to make sure it does work - we've just missed each other.  Evelyn at Cheetah was a very nice person to deal with, and it is obvious that Cheetah does care about their products and the reputation of the company.    So, for that, I give them 2 more stars!    Kudos!

review_headline: Comfortable and VERY EASY to Assemble
review_body:

I wanted to take a moment to speak about the assembly process because I was concerned after reading so many comments complaining about the complexity in performing this task. I was able to assemble this chair in a matter of 15 minutes! Here are some tricks to consider:

1. There is a link to an assembly demonstration on the Amazon page. Look at how the gentlemen is performing the task and follow it exactly and you will have quick results as well

2. I followed the instructions including using the packaging box as a work platform. I think this is key because it allows you to position the back and seat on a level surface while assembling the arms, etc.

3. I have a ratchet type screwdriver that works with \\"drill\\" bits. I found the bit that corresponded to the allen wrench provided in the screw packet and used that in lieu of the wrench. I think this made the process much easier.

Bottom line: easy assembly and a great chair for the price!

review_headline: For the price it can't be beat!
review_body:
I bought this primarily for my dad. Fortunately, I had a similar size screw without a nut and just assembled one side without the nut. This was because I had a broken office chair and kept the assembling screws before I tossed the chair.

I was wheezing with asthma and still was able to assemble this chair in under a hour, so there is no excuse for people not to assemble this themselves.

Bonus was there was a piece of plywood in the box which I used it to put my himalayan salt lamp by my table. Everything now is from China anyways so I can't mark a star off for that.

For the price of the chair when I bought it I cannot complain about it since it also goes well with the rest of the decor and brown furniture in my modest living room apartment.

review_headline: Not as good as Thousand Oaks Barrels
review_body: I requested this barrel as a Christmas gift. It arrived later than expected. I would have been fine with that, if it were top quality. But...it's not. Several of the slats used to make the barrel were all marked up, rather than smooth. The spigot seemed to be flimsy. When I tried to season the barrel, it kept leaking quickly. Upon further inspection, there were two holes in one of the slats: no amount of seasoning was going to close those. Finally: I'm wary of the shellac or wax or whatever it is they put on the outside of this barrel. All the other home-aging barrels I've purchased in the past have been bare wood, and I've aged some fantastic whiskey in them. I don't know why this one is sealed on the outside. In any case, if you're a home-ager and thinking that this is a good and Amazon-ready equivalent to the Thousand Oaks products...this is not equivalent. Lesson learned for me.

product_title: Coaster 3pc Coffee Table & End Table Set Faux Marble Top Espresso Finish
review_headline: The worst manufacturing-shipping of a particle board product that ...
review_body: Do yourself a favor:  Don't buy it!  I should have taken the advise of others who purchased this table set, but thought \\"maybe\\" they've made improvements -- Not the case!    First, the vendor (Moshya Home Furnishings) lost the first set when, after two weeks, I noticed there was no movement on the tracking via Amazon.  I contacted Moshya and they apologized sending a second set which arrived two days ago.  There was no external damage to the box (shipped UPS), but the weight of the box was just under 100 pounds, and the damage WAS quite apparent once I carefully opened the box and removed each component.    This is the worst manufacturing and shipping of a particle board product that I've seen in over 40 years; production of particle board items has improved significantly over the years, but not in this product, manufactured in China.    I had to purchase the following from the local home improvement store to fix all three tables incident to assembly:  Two bottles of wood glue, a box (of 50) 1\\" particle board screws, and a set of touch-up furniture pens.  ALL three table frames were detached from their tops:  Not only did the wood glue fail, but all of the screws holding the frames to the tops had pulled-loose during shipping, some screws were even found loose in the shipping box.    Day 1 of assembly:  Re-glue the frames to the tops; drill and install new screws between the frame and the table tops; leave wood glue to dry and set overnight.    Day 2 of assembly:  Install the provided parts (mostly screws with washers); touch-up all of the nicks located on the legs, frames, and sides.  The only saving grace:  The table tops were not damaged or scratched.  However it took quite some time to inspect each table so I could touch-up gouges, nicks, and scratches located elsewhere (and visible) with a purchased set of furniture touch-up pens.    I had high hopes for this set, but i do NOT recommend it.  Had it been easy to re-pack this \\"junk\\", I would have sent it back fora refund, but instead I'm hoping either Amazon or their sub-seller, Moshya Home Furnishings, will provide a partial refund.    UPDATE 1/26/2015:  Amazon's vendor, Moshya Home Furnishings is providing me with a 15% refund based on photos of the damage and information I provided them. A partial refund is better than none!

product_title: Sauder Harbor View Library, Antiqued White
review_headline: Nice bookcase; here are some tips to make assembly easier.
review_body:
I bought this to coordinate with a French writing desk I inherited. I'm very happy with the bookcase. To gauge my skills, I'm fairly handy but not a pro. All told, it probably took me, without assistance, 3 hours over a day or two to complete assembly, including the extra steps I took, described below. I used a variable speed drill with phillips attachment for most of the project (but kept my drill speed on the low side), and sometimes a manual #2 phillips. My advice: take your time and read the instructions through beforehand so you know what to expect. Take breaks if (when) frustrated. You can do this!
The long side facings on my unit were broken when I unpacked the box. I suggest going through the hardware bag to ensure you have all the hardware you need before contacting Sauder. The instruction booklet tells you how many pieces of each type of hardware you should have. I was missing a few pieces of hardware and was able to have those shipped with the new side facings.
While assembling, I found it difficult to get underneath the unit to attach the screws to the side facings while keeping the facings in place. You are really working \\"upside down\\" and attaching pieces from below, and it's very difficult to see what you're doing. My solution was to first glue the side facings onto the front of the bookcase (a 1/8\\" bead of carpenter's glue on each surface is all you need); spread the glue around and apply the facing. MAKE SURE you place these facings the correct way as shown in the instructions, so the scored line on the back of the facing runs through the screw holes on the brown plastic connectors. You can use a mirror to check this. No need to clamp but you will need to wait several hours for glue drying. Then you can attach the screws after you flip the bookcase over, and the side facings will stay in place. This extra step takes time, but improves accuracy and makes that part of the task much easier. Also, if you are using this approach, you can minimally attach the front top arch with the screws first, and finish attaching the arch when you flip the bookcase.
Make sure you have enough working room to complete assembly of the bookcase, because you must flip the bookcase over in mid-assembly.
When attaching the back, I advise to ensure each nail hole on the front (finished) side is punched through to the back prior to attachment. On mine, some small nail holes did not go through to the back so I had to remove the back and repunch the holes. The back is dark brown and it's difficult to see the holes if they are not punched through.
If you can avoid it, don't punch through the \\"handholds\\" on the back unless you really need them. I was able to pick up the bookcase myself without using the handholds but had already punched one partially out. I can't imagine why the handholds are there--the backing is very thin and I could feel the small brad nails that hold the back to the bookcase coming loose when I attempted to use the handhold. If anything the handhold might be used for leverage, but I advise not to place any pressure on the handhold.
When attaching the feet, I initially had problems turning the foot screw into the foot. I then used a pliers to hold the screw stable while turning the screw onto the foot. That worked much better. You just need to get it started straight; then when you screw the foot into the bottom of the unit, your leverage will do the rest.
Don't forget: there's no scratch protection on the bottom of the unit. If you are assembling this unit to be placed on a wood floor, be sure to place felt furniture pads on the bottoms of the feet and the back. You can buy these self stick pads at any home improvement store. Each foot takes a 1 ½\\" round felt pad, and the back takes a 3\\" x ¾\\" rectangle.
I have a lot of books, and it's not difficult to reach the suggested weight limits of 25 to 40 lbs. with big art books. I weighed the stacks of bookson the bathroom scale before placing them, so as not to exceed the weight limits.
The completed bookcase is very functional and looks a lot more expensive than it is. (Well, that probably depends upon how you value your time and frustration.) For me, it was worth it. I might order another one!

review_headline: Amazon had the best price and fastest deliver (in stock delivered in 3 ...
review_body:
Was a bit skeptical about ordering this sight unseen. Amazon had the best price and fastest deliver (in stock delivered in 3 days) plus with prime it was a no brainer. Our bed arrived in one big box. Well packed and protected. There was one overall set of instructions on top of everything that illustrated the entire bed assembly in 10 easy to follow steps. All quantities of hardware matched the build sheet and no pieces were missing. Took me about 1.5 hours to assemble alone.

I have seen several reviews mentioning, nail head strips, gaps in panels, headboard/mattress gaps etc. Our bed had one area where the parts didnt align. One of the front corners where the panels meet are off a little its on the lower edge so you have to look for it to notice. There would be a gap if we had a thinner mattress at the headboard however both the bed a mattress were bought at the same time at took this into account. We have a simmons recharge 13.5" bed and 9" box spring and it is tall enough to go above the bottom edge of the headboard. Every nail in our bed is individual and separated by a few mm. There is some "give" at the very top of the headboard where it meets the wall. review_body: I spent a lot of time researching and trying to find the perfect CD rack. This one is pretty good. I believe it will hold around 360 CDs on the bottom 9 racks (around 40 per shelf), and an additional 30 or so on the top rack if you stack them horizontally. This piece does have a design flaw in my opinion with that top rack. The top moulding comes down too far and you wouldn't be able to get to any CDs you would place there vertically, unless you left lots of room. You CAN leave off that piece of top moulding, and if you were handy you could paint the bare wood black to match or cut down that top piece of moulding to make it give you more room. I haven't decided what I'll do yet. I have some large box set pieces that I think I'll put there to use the space. You could put DVDs or cassettes or knick knacks or whatever else. It just won't fit a CD vertically and able to pull it out straight with that piece of moulding on. Also another small problem is the side mouldings obscure about 2 CDs on either side. I plan to just put empty jewel cases there to take up space. You could put a little piece of cardboard or something else. It's not a huge problem for me since I'm not taking up every inch of space (yet). It does come with a wall anchor so you can anchor it to the wall, and the bottom piece is longer in the front to make it nice and stable. The color is a rich black and it arrived perfect with no dings or scratches. The only other small gripe I have is that the back plate is a tad too small to fit to be able to put the nails in the way it describes. What I did is I centered it perfectly on the back of the piece while it laid face down on my floor and I taped it in place. That way when I nailed it on the veeeeeery edge of the back plate, it stayed in place and didn't move. It comes with a black marker to fix any dings I guess, but I didn't need it. I'm including a photo with a CD in the top shelf so you can see how much room is taken away from you. I hope you enjoy it!

product_title: Winsome Wood Foldable Desk, Natural
review_body:
This desk is very easy to put together: four screws, and you're done with assembly except for sliding the keyboard drawer into place.

Now, I am mechanically reclined, not inclined, so it took me a few times of screwing it up to get that keyboard drawer oriented correctly. But once that happened, everything worked quite well.

Earlier reivewers stated that the desk was a little too unstable for their tastes, but I haven't experienced that. (It may be that the mfr. has attached a rail to the underside of newer models which acts as a leg stop. Mine has them.) I did buy a pair of window latches, as one reviewer suggested, but I'm having a little trouble thinking through where to attach them.

It's true that the desk is a little more willing to move side-to-side than I would prefer, but as it's not in a high-traffic area or used by rambunctious persons, I feel fine about waiting to resolve that problem in a way that maintains the desk's collapsability.

That said, I don't know that I'd choose it for a pre-teen's room. A slight case of the fragiles aside, it's an adult-scale desk.

The wood, and it is all wood, got one thin coat of varnish and could stand another. The top is constructed of narrow strips of varying colors; some gradations of color are quite abrupt.

In short, it's not a showpiece, but it is a workable, serviceable desk with few unresolvable problems, and an attractive appearance.

product_title: My Comfy Table
review_headline: Table Surface Angle May Be an Issue
review_body:
I bought this table as a Laptop table. It will work for my purposes but that's only because I'm using it primarily as a Laptop table for viewing with the DVD Drive and am rarely using the keyboard when away from the house.

Pros:

- It is portable and folds up well as advertised for storage under furniture and for mobility.
- Setup and height adjustment are easy and fast.

Cons:

- The biggest point is that the table top isn't level as has been indicated by other reviewers, When the table is oriented as designed, with the legs pointing toward the chair, the table top inclines slightly. I'd estimate the inclination angle is approx 5° so the top is angled up towards the user. For my purposes it's not a deal breaker but my product rating isn't higher based the fact that the product description doesn't mention that the top surface isn't level.

- The table isn't very sturdy but it will work for serving a snack or small meal. My view is that it's not sturdy enough to use for typing on a Laptop. I have one of the older model (heavier and thicker) Laptop's, weighing about 5.5 Lbs so this table may work ok for the newer-generation thinner Laptop's and Tablets.

Bottom line for me is that due to the low price and that I got this table for a limited purpose, I'm keeping it but I'd advise others to look for a better-made product. However for this price, it's hard to complain too much :)

I gave it 3 stars but barely, and only because I can use it for my specific purpose.

[edit] Well, after spending more time using my Laptop with this table, I wanted to update this review. I'm more satisfied with this table than my original assessment. The table surface leveled ok with my Laptop sitting on it but that's mainly due to the weight of my Laptop which is about 5.5 Lbs.

That effectively leveled my tabletop surface so that it's no longer angling upward facing the chair/couch.

I updated my rating to 4 stars but wished the Mfgr had included this in its product description:

With the table assembled with nothing placed on the table surface (or light-weight items), the table surface is not level. It angles upward toward the chair.
